properties.description: Inside Out (2015), directed by Pete Docter, is a Pixar animated adventure-drama starring Amy Poehler, Bill Hader and Lewis Black that personifies a child's emotions as they navigate a major life change. The film follows a young girl who moves to a new city and the emotional turmoil inside her as Joy, Sadness, Fear, Disgust and Anger contend over how to cope. Combining family-friendly comedy with psychological depth, it explores memory, grief, identity and emotional regulation through inventive visual metaphors and a bittersweet emotional core.
properties.plot_summary: When a young girl is uprooted from her Midwestern home and moves to a new city, the personified emotions that run her inner life — Joy, Sadness, Fear, Disgust and Anger — struggle to guide her through the upheaval. As Joy tries to keep everything positive, unexpected combinations of memories and Sadness’s influence force the emotions to confront how core memories shape identity. The story follows an emotional journey through imaginative inner landscapes and memory stores as the girl learns to accept complicated feelings and rebuilds her sense of self and family connection.

properties.description: Youth (2015), directed by Paolo Sorrentino and starring Michael Caine, Harvey Keitel and Rachel Weisz, is an art-house comedy-drama with strong musical elements. Set mainly in the Swiss Alps, it follows a retired conductor whose invitation to perform for royalty catalyzes conversations about memory, friendship, artistic legacy and the compromises of a long life. The film mixes elegiac, often humorous exchanges with striking visual compositions and music-driven sequences to explore aging, regret and the value of the present. Overall it delivers a contemplative, emotionally resonant experience aimed at reflective viewers.
properties.plot_summary: A retired orchestra conductor is vacationing in the Swiss Alps with his daughter and his longtime film-director friend when he receives an invitation from the Queen to perform for Prince Philip's birthday. The visit and the impending performance prompt quiet, probing conversations about art, memory, past accomplishments and what it means to live well in old age. Interwoven episodes — including encounters with younger characters, a symbolic beauty-pageant presence and the slow revelation of his wife's deteriorated condition — force each character to reckon with regret, desire and the value of the present.

properties.description: Room (2015), directed by Lenny Abrahamson and adapted for the screen by Emma Donoghue from her novel, is a drama-thriller starring Brie Larson, Jacob Tremblay and Sean Bridgers. It follows a mother and her young son who have been held in a single locked room for years and the fraught, painful process that follows their escape. The film centers on the psychological aftermath of captivity, the resilience of the parent-child bond, and the difficulty of reclaiming a life beyond confinement. Intense performances and a restrained, claustrophobic style create an emotionally powerful and often unsettling experience.
properties.plot_summary: A young boy has spent his entire life confined to a single locked room with his mother, who was abducted years earlier. She has raised him within the cramped space, teaching him to read and shaping the room as his whole world. When the truth about their captivity is revealed and they attempt to escape, both must confront physical danger and the deep psychological wounds of imprisonment. The story follows their fraught transition from confinement toward recovery and reintegration.

Thematically it interrogates institutional power, clerical abuse and the responsibilities of the press, delivering a measured, emotionally affecting account of accountability and trauma.
properties.plot_summary: A Boston Globe investigative team follows a trail of sealed records, reluctant sources, and institutional stonewalling to uncover decades of child sexual abuse and systematic cover-up within the local Catholic Archdiocese. The investigation tests the reporters' methods, ethics and resolve while centering the experiences and trauma of the victims whose stories had been suppressed.

properties.description: Me and Earl and the Dying Girl (2015), directed by Alfonso Gomez-Rejon and adapted by Jesse Andrews from his novel, is an indie comedy-drama starring Thomas Mann, RJ Cyler, and Olivia Cooke. A self-protective teen who makes parody films is pushed into an uneasy friendship with a classmate diagnosed with leukemia; their relationship forces him to confront attachment, creativity, and mortality. The movie mixes sharp, ironic humor and film-referential pastiche with tender, character-driven drama to explore friendship, growth, and the ethics of care.
properties.plot_summary: A self-protective high-schooler who spends his time making parody films with a friend avoids real attachment until his mother insists he spend time with a classmate recently diagnosed with leukemia. Reluctant visits turn into a complicated, genuine friendship that forces him to confront his habitual detachment. Their bond pushes him to translate his filmmaking into something sincere and to face questions of loyalty, mortality, and identity. The film balances sharp, deadpan humor with tender, affecting emotional beats.

properties.description: The Lobster (2015), directed by Yorgos Lanthimos and co-written with Efthimis Filippou, is a dystopian drama/romantic science fiction thriller starring Colin Farrell, Rachel Weisz and Jessica Barden. Set at a government-run hotel where singles have forty-five days to find a partner or be transformed into animals and exiled, the film uses absurdist satire and deadpan performances to interrogate conformity and the politics of intimacy. Its tone is bleak yet darkly comic, pairing formal, restrained visual design with provocative examinations of identity, love, and authoritarian social control.
properties.plot_summary: In a dystopian near future, single people are sent to a government-run hotel where they must find a romantic partner within forty-five days or be surgically transformed into an animal and expelled into the surrounding woods. The system enforces arbitrary compatibility rules and punishes nonconformity, while a fugitive contingent of ‘loners’ survive outside the city under strict, oppositional rules. The story follows a newly arrived man as he navigates the hotel’s ritualized dating, the moral compromises it requires, and the bleakly absurd consequences of choosing love or freedom.

properties.description: Victoria (2015), directed by Sebastian Schipper and starring Laia Costa, Frederick Lau and Franz Rogowski, is a German one-shot crime drama and romantic thriller that unfolds over a single night in Berlin. The film follows a recently arrived Spanish woman whose flirtation with a local man draws her into a circle of petty criminals and, ultimately, a dangerous heist. Shot in one continuous take, the movie emphasizes real-time character development, language friction, loneliness, and the moral consequences of desperate choices. Its tone is immersive and tense, alternating between playful camaraderie and escalating dread.
properties.plot_summary: A young Spanish woman who has recently moved to Berlin drifts into the city’s nightlife and is taken under the wing of a group of local men. What begins as flirtation and camaraderie gradually deepens into a romantic connection with one member and, later, into complicity in a dangerous criminal plan. The night unfolds in real time as playful moments and language barriers give way to escalating tension, moral compromise, and violent consequences.

properties.audience_identity: Cinephiles and thoughtful viewers drawn to immersive, formally daring films who value intense character-driven stories, urban realism, and moral ambiguity over spectacle.
properties.genre_description: A character-driven urban thriller that blends crime and romantic drama elements, unfolding in real time to emphasize immediacy and moral escalation.
properties.style_description: Shot as a continuous real-time take, the film uses handheld, naturalistic camerawork and intimate staging to create an immersive, documentary-like experience.

properties.plot_themes_description: The story probes loneliness and shattered dreams against the backdrop of urban life and immigration, showing how belonging and language gaps can lead to risky alliances and criminal consequences.

properties.description: 'Als wir träumten' (2015), directed by Andreas Dresen and adapted from Clemens Meyer's novel with a screenplay by Wolfgang Kohlhaase, stars Merlin Rose, Julius Nitschkoff and Joel Basman. This drama follows a group of friends in early 1990s Leipzig who create a techno club after reunification and gradually descend into drinking, drugs, violence and crime. The film explores themes of disillusionment, friendship and identity with a gritty, melancholic tone and an episodic, chaptered structure. Its raw, socially grounded realism emphasizes the emotional cost of sudden freedom and social collapse.
properties.plot_summary: In early 1990s Leipzig, a group of teenage friends obsessed with techno build a club as a refuge from the chaos of reunification. Nights of music and revelry escalate into shoplifting, vandalism, clashes with rival gangs and skinheads, and increasing substance abuse. The film follows how freedom without guidance and mounting social dislocation drive the protagonists into crime, incarceration, and premature ruin, tracing a bleak coming‑of‑age arc.

properties.style_description: Gritty and atmospheric, the film pairs strobe-lit club sequences with raw, documentary-like intimacy and an episodic, chaptered structure to portray a bleak urban youth experience.
